entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: On the above aspect, Mr. Ranjit kumar, learned Senior Counsel would advert to similar kind of prayer made in I.A. No.124085/2020 and then submits that the said I.A. No. 124085/2020 was considered consecutively on 30.07.2021, 05.10.2021 and finally in the judgment delivered this Court on 14.12.2021, the contempt petitions were dismissed under the Signed order and in that proceeding all the pending applications including IA No.124085/2020 were also disposed of.

In the order passed by this Court on 17.08.2015 in Civil Appeal Nos. 10394-10396/2011, this Court permitted the respondent- State to initiate fresh acquisition proceedings having noted the fact that the State failed to comply with Section 11A proceedings under the old Land Acquisition Act 1894.

Moreover, once possession of the concerned land was taken by the State under Section 17 of the Land Acquisition Act 1894, it is no longer open to the State to relinquish or return the land to the legal entity who had been dispossessed of such land.

sentences.text: We have considered the rival submission of the learned Senior Counsel for the parties.
The proceedings of this Court recorded on 14.12.2021 holding the respondents to be not in contempt of the previous orders passed by this Court, are also noted by us.

On the possibility of the ousted land owners getting higher compensation, we find that the Court had protected this aspect by adverting to the provisions of Section 64 and Section 74 of the  3 2013 Act.
The Court also made it clear that it had not expressed any opinion either on the categorization of the land or on determination of the market value in the Award dated 12.11.2020.

Taking all the aforesaid circumstances into account and particularly having regard to the opinion expressed by this Court in the contempt proceeding and I.A No.124085/2020 and the further fact that the land owners have received compensation, albeit under protest, to the tune of Rs.99.03 Crores, we see no reason to pass any order in the I.A. No.4705/2022 in M.A. Diary No.1395/2022 and the same stands dismissed.
Accordingly, the Miscellaneous Application stands disposed of.

As reference under Section 64 is to be made within six weeks from the date of the collectors Award, the time spent by the petitioners in pursuing the present litigation through the M.A.
Diary No(s).
1395/2022 should be discounted by the Reference Court while adjudicating the Reference Application proposed to be moved by the applicants.

Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of M/S Soorajmull Nagarmull vs Sri Brijesh Mehrotra on 13 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33834420/
